meta.name: Scan Japanese tech news for market-entry signals and notify Slack

name: Scan Japanese news for market-entry demand signals

parameters.content:
## Japan market demand-signal scanner — zero-cost, no API key required

This workflow helps you get a *directional* read on whether an overseas service (once described in Japanese) is showing up in Japanese news / press releases — useful as a first pass before deciding whether to invest in formal market research for a Japan launch. It searches three major Japanese news/press-release feeds for your keywords and returns the actual matching articles as structured data (title, link, date, source) plus a plain-language summary — with no AI step and no API key/credential of any kind required. It never claims "no results" means "no demand".

### Try it
Send a POST request with a JSON body such as:
`{"serviceName": "Acme Expense OCR", "keywordsJa": ["経費精算", "領収書 OCR", "インボイス制度 対応"], "competitorNamesJa": ["マネーフォワード クラウド経費"]}`

keywordsJa is required (Japanese search terms — the feeds are Japanese-language, so English keywords will not match). competitorNamesJa and serviceDescription are optional.

### Before you activate
(Optional) Create a Slack Incoming Webhook and paste its URL into the "Set: Slack webhook URL" node — Slack is only notified when actual matching articles are found. Nothing else is required; there is no external API cost to run this workflow.

### Known limitation
This checks 3 fixed Japanese news/press-release feeds (see Step 2). It returns raw matching articles, not an AI-written interpretation — read the linked articles yourself to judge relevance. It is a lightweight directional scan, not a substitute for paid market research, surveys, or industry reports.

Step 1 — Receive & validate

Accepts the incoming webhook POST request. Requires serviceName and a non-empty keywordsJa array of Japanese search terms. competitorNamesJa and serviceDescription are optional. Invalid requests get an immediate 400 response instead of reaching the feeds.

Step 2 — Fetch 3 Japanese news feeds

Fetches ITmedia ビジネスオンライン, Impress Watch and PR TIMES — all official RSS/RDF feeds, no API key needed. If a feed fails to fetch, it's skipped rather than failing the whole run. Swap in different feed URLs here if you want different sources or a different industry focus.

Step 3 — Filter by keyword & build the response

Extracts articles via lightweight regex parsing (works across both RSS 2.0 and RDF/RSS 1.0 without depending on a specific XML-to-JSON node's nesting behavior), keeps only the ones whose title/description contain one of your keywords, and writes a plain-language (non-AI) summary of what was found — or an honest "nothing found" message if there were no matches.

Step 4 — Respond & notify Slack

Always returns a JSON response to the caller (matching articles + summary message, or an honest no-matches message, or a structured validation error). When at least one article matched, a preview is also posted to Slack via an Incoming Webhook in parallel — the "no matches" case does not post to Slack, to avoid noise.

nodes.name: Fetch ITmedia Business feed
nodes.notes: Official ITmedia RSS feed list confirmed at https://corp.itmedia.co.jp/media/rss_list/ (checked 2026-08-18). If this feed fails to fetch, it is skipped rather than failing the whole run (see "Parse & filter articles").

nodes.name: Fetch Impress Watch feed
nodes.notes: Official Impress Watch RSS feed, confirmed live 2026-08-18. If this feed fails to fetch, it is skipped rather than failing the whole run.

nodes.name: Fetch PR TIMES feed
nodes.notes: Official PR TIMES all-releases RDF feed, confirmed live 2026-08-18 (high volume, useful for catching new-service launch announcements). If this feed fails to fetch, it is skipped rather than failing the whole run.

nodes.name: Parse & filter articles
nodes.notes: Extracts <item> blocks via regex directly from the raw XML text (rather than relying on an XML-to-JSON node's nesting behavior) so the same code works for both RSS 2.0 (ITmedia) and RDF/RSS 1.0 (Impress Watch, PR TIMES) without needing to verify each format's parsed JSON shape separately.

nodes.name: Build response
nodes.notes: No AI step — this writes a plain-language summary directly from the matched (or not matched) article data using template strings only.

nodes.name: Matches found?
nodes.notes: Only routes to Slack when at least one article matched, to avoid posting a "nothing found" message every time the workflow runs.

nodes.name: Set: Slack webhook URL
nodes.notes: Placeholder value — not a real webhook URL. Create your own Slack Incoming Webhook (Slack > your app > Incoming Webhooks) and paste the URL here before activating. No Slack app OAuth setup beyond that is required. Entirely optional — the workflow's HTTP response works without this.

nodes.name: Notify Slack
nodes.notes: continueOnFail=true so a placeholder or misconfigured Slack URL never affects the caller's response — the webhook has already responded independently by this point.
